hook.line: A board game found ready to play in a Mesopotamian royal tomb — one of the oldest games whose rules we know.
hook.say: Let me show you the game of kings!

ch.t: From the Royal Tombs of Ur
ch.say: The boards came out of the sand intact.
p: At Tell al-Muqayyar in southern Iraq — ancient Ur — Leonard Woolley excavated the Royal Cemetery in 1922–34 and found five boards.
Boards of the same kind turned up in Iran, Syria, Egypt, Cyprus, Crete and far-off Sri Lanka, and the game reached Kochi in India.

tl: Boards are buried in the royal tombs of Ur
Tutankhamun’s tomb holds game boxes with senet on the other side
A board is scratched on a winged bull at an Assyrian palace
The scribe Itti-Marduk-balāṭu writes the rules on a clay tablet
Woolley excavates the Royal Cemetery at Ur
Kochi’s Jewish community plays it as “Aasha”
Irving Finkel of the British Museum deciphers the tablet
RoyalUr announces the best move for every position

ch.say: Land on a flower and roll again!
ch.cap: The 20-square board with five rosettes. The arrows show the near player’s track
p: Enter on your own four squares, race down the middle row, and finish through your last two. Land on a rival in the middle row to capture it.
The British Museum board (ME 120834) is inlaid with shell, lapis lazuli and red limestone set in bitumen.

ch.say: Rules changed with time and place.
cards: Seven pieces each and four pyramid dice — the most played today
A descendant of the 20-square board, played with 12 pieces each
The same family of board, on the back of senet boards
Landing on squares meant things like “you will find a friend”, “you will become powerful like a lion” or “you will draw fine beer”
The tablet came from the ruins of Babylon and went to the British Museum
Pyramids (tetrahedra). Two of the four tips are marked; count the marked tips that point up
A gate guardian at an Assyrian palace bears a board, probably carved by bored guards
In 2025 RoyalUr announced the best move for all of about 276 million positions

ch.say: Play the same game as the kings!
p: Aim for the flowers and trust your dice.
